correctness.rationale: The claim is finite and fully exhaustive. The verifier reconstructs all \(120\) permutations, all \(5340\) compatibility edges, enumerates every maximal clique, finds maximum size \(10\) and exactly \(192\) maxima, then exhausts all \(240\) specified isometries and recomputes all \(45\) pair distances in representatives. No timeout, random sampling, or extrapolation is used. The claim is restricted to the displayed natural subgroup, avoiding an unsupported full-automorphism assertion.

evidence: The 2024 Bereg--Haghpanah--Malouf--Sudborough result gives \(P(n,n-2)=10\) for \(n\ge5\), hence covers only the size component.
The 2025 Bereg--Miller--Sudborough paper explicitly cites that exact-size theorem and proves \(R(n;2,2)=10\) for \(n\ge5\).
broader_coverage.reasoning: These stronger parameter-range results establish the optimum size but do not determine how many maximum codes occur or how they decompose under the displayed finite isometry action. Therefore they do not imply the accepted structural claim.

originality.rationale: The exact optimum \(P(5,3)=10\) is prior and is not treated as original. The accepted contribution is the complete labeled extremizer census (\(192\)) and its three-orbit decomposition under the natural \(240\)-element isometry subgroup. Exact-parameter and alias searches, together with inspection of the foundational, 2024 exact-size, and 2025 upper-bound papers, found no statement implying that census or orbit data.
residual_risks: An unindexed thesis, supplementary computation, or unpublished finite census could have enumerated the same 192 maxima.
The natural 240-element subgroup is intentionally not asserted to be the full automorphism group, so no originality claim is made about full-isometry classification.

value.rationale: The case \(n=5\) is the smallest case in the exact family \(P(n,n-2)=10\) for \(n\ge5\), making the full extremizer structure a natural base-case invariant rather than an arbitrary slice. The result separates all maxima into three symmetry types with distinct internal distance spectra, information not supplied by the known exact-size theorem and useful for testing structural conjectures or recursive constructions in Chebyshev permutation coding.
